module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 424: Sequence generated by $a_i a_j - 1$

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424)
 - [A5244](https://oeis.org/A5244)
 - [Ben Green's Open Problem 63](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8 Problem 63)
 - [Ko26] Korsky, S., *A problem of Erdős on the sequence $a_ia_j - 1$*,
   [arXiv:2608.07910](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07910)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos424

open Set

/--
Defines the set of new numbers generated from a set A by the operation
$x y - 1$ for $x \neq y$.
-/
def nextGeneration (A : Set ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  { z : ℕ | ∃ x y, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ A ∧ x ≠ y ∧ z = x * y - 1 }

/--
The sequence of sets $A_n$ where $A_0 = \{2, 3\}$ and $A_{n+1}$ is $A_n$ union all newly
generated elements.
-/
def sequenceSet : ℕ → Set ℕ
  | 0 => {2, 3}
  | n + 1 => (sequenceSet n) ∪ (nextGeneration (sequenceSet n))

/-- The set of integers which eventually appear in the sequence, which is the union of all $A_n$. -/
def generatedSet : Set ℕ := ⋃ n : ℕ, sequenceSet n

/--
Let $a_1 = 2$ and $a_2 = 3$ and continue the sequence by appending to $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ all possible
values of $a_i a_j - 1$ with $i \neq j$.
Is it true that the set of integers which eventually appear has positive density?

As explained on [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424), "positive density"
here means positive *lower* density: is there $c > 0$ such that for all large $x$ at least
$cx$ of the integers in $[1, x]$ appear? See `erdos_424.variants.exact_density` for the
literal reading.

The answer is yes: Korsky [Ko26] (with ChatGPT 5.6 Pro) proved that the set has positive lower
density. The linked formal proof (Alexeev and Codex) shows that there is `c > 0` with
`c * x ≤ #{n ∈ [1, x] | n ∈ generatedSet}` for all large `x`, which gives
`c / 2 ≤ generatedSet.lowerDensity`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos424.lean#L6409"]
theorem erdos_424 : answer(True) ↔ 0 < generatedSet.lowerDensity := by
  sorry

/--
A literal interpretation of "positive density": the natural density of `generatedSet` exists
(i.e. the lower and upper density agree) and is positive.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_424.variants.exact_density : answer(sorry) ↔ generatedSet.HasPosDensity := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): formalize the statements from the additional material

end Erdos424

findings.description: The module docstring's reference [Ko26] has the wrong title. It reads "Korsky, S., *A problem of Erdős on the sequence $a_ia_j - 1$*, arXiv:2608.07910", but arXiv:2608.07910 (v1, the only version) is titled "Positive Lower Density for Hofstadter's $ab-1$ Problem". Author, id and content are right; only the title is wrong. The mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07910: "[2608.07910] Positive Lower Density for Hofstadter's $ab-1$ Problem", Samuel Korsky, submitted 8 Aug 2026. The e-print source Hofstadter.tex has \title{Positive Lower Density for Hofstadter's $ab-1$ Problem}.
findings.suggested_fix: [Ko26] Korsky, S., *Positive Lower Density for Hofstadter's $ab-1$ Problem*, [arXiv:2608.07910](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07910)

reformulations.difference: The source (erdosproblems.com/424) states the intended reading as "does there exist c>0 such that for all large x the number of values of a_i in [1,x] is at least cx?". The Lean states `0 < generatedSet.lowerDensity`, i.e. 0 < liminf_{b→∞} #(S ∩ [0,b))/b. The linked formal proof concludes `∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, c*x ≤ #((Icc 1 x).filter (· ∈ generatedSet))`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every S : Set ℕ I proved in Lean `0 < S.lowerDensity ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, c * x ≤ #{n ∈ [1,x] | n ∈ S}`. (→): eventually partialDensity > L/2, so #(S∩[1,x]) ≥ (L/2)(x+1) − 1 ≥ (L/4)x for large x. (←): partialDensity(x+1) ≥ c·x/(x+1) ≥ c/2, then `le_liminf_of_le`. Moving between real and natural x changes c by at most a factor of 2. I also combined the linked formal proof (compiled locally, standard axioms only) with this lemma. That gives a full Lean proof of the FC statement `True ↔ 0 < Erdos424.generatedSet.lowerDensity`, after showing its verbatim copies of `sequenceSet`/`generatedSet` equal the FC ones.

reformulations.difference: The source says "append all possible values of a_i a_j − 1 with i ≠ j", a condition on indices. The Lean requires distinct values x ≠ y and takes the union of finite stages of the closure.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The source's sequence lists each integer once ("2,3,5,9,14,17,26,..."; OEIS A005244, whose Mathematica code uses Subsets[s,{2}]), so distinct indices means distinct values. Allowing repeated values would add 24 = 5·5−1, which the source's listing omits. I proved in Lean that 8 ∉ generatedSet and 24 ∉ generatedSet. A computable mirror of the Lean rule reproduces the OEIS data exactly up to 249 (checked with #eval). Korsky's paper and the formal proof use the same smallest-closed-set notion; the formal proof shows the staged union equals that inductive closure.

review.notes:
Both declarations match the source.

1. `erdos_424` (`answer(True) ↔ 0 < generatedSet.lowerDensity`, research solved): the set, the lower-density reading (the one erdosproblems.com says Erdős most likely meant), the answer's polarity and the formal_proof record are all correct. The linked formal proof (plby/lean-proofs @8822f7dd, anchor #L6409 = `theorem erdos_424`) compiled locally on Lean v4.33.1 + Mathlib; `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and there is no sorry, native_decide or axiom. Bridged through my `lowerDensity_pos_iff`, it proves the exact FC statement.

2. `erdos_424.variants.exact_density` (natural density exists and is positive, `answer(sorry)`, research open): this is a faithful statement of the literal reading. Nothing in the sources shows the density exists, so `open` is right.

Status note, not reported as a status issue: erdosproblems.com still shows 424 as "OPEN" (accessed 2026-09-23), and the teorth database says "open" (last_update 2025-08-31). The forum lists Korsky's full proof claim (2026-07-20), and Alexeev's comment confirms the Lean formalization. The file's `research solved` is justified under CONTRIBUTING's rule ("formally proved here or elsewhere"). The file is ahead of the site, not stale.

Aside on another file (not under review): Green's Problem 63 says "a_1a_2 − 1 ∈ A if a_1, a_2 ∈ A", with no distinctness. That gives a different set (it contains 8 = 3·3−1 and 24 = 5·5−1). FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/63.lean says it points to this file's formalization, which uses x ≠ y. That is faithful to Erdős [Er77c], as Korsky's partial claim notes. It may deserve a remark in the Green file.

I could not read [Er77c] (scanned) or [ErGr80] (download failed) directly. I relied on erdosproblems.com's and Korsky's descriptions of them, which agree with each other.
